title: Decouple delivery health observations from the maintenance CAS

owned: Delivery health observation commit path in .orchestrator/supervisor.py: commit_delivery_health_observations() and the run_once() call site that runs it ahead of, and independently of, the maintenance phase
Sustained reserved-phase discard visibility: record_reserved_phase_outcome() per-phase consecutive-discard streak tracking and the console_log escalation past SUSTAINED_PHASE_DISCARD_THRESHOLD
not_changing: Existing guard semantics for worker and queue transitions inside _run_reserved_runtime_phase (unchanged)
apply_post_dispatch_maintenance's own transition logic (unchanged; it now simply receives delivery_health_observations=() because those observations are committed earlier)
Topology reconcile, which still runs after maintenance and still observes the health writes because that phase reloads runtime state
composes_with: OPS-FENCED-WORKER-QUEUE-PROOF-001 (removed the worst discard trigger but left this CAS coupling in place; this task removes the coupling itself)

failure_reproduction.case: Delivery health is read-only evidence about a provider endpoint. It took part in no worker or queue transition, but was committed inside the maintenance phase's single reserved-phase transaction, so any unrelated transition that transaction could not prove (a queue record the guard could not justify, a worker whose exact completion event had not landed) also discarded that cycle's health probe results.
failure_reproduction.prior_outcome: delivery_health.evidence_ttl_seconds is 300s live. A sustained discard rate expires every lane's health evidence; the dispatcher then refuses every lane with HEALTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED, and no worker is left to change the state that would end the stall. Measured 2026-09-17 after the worst trigger (OPS-FENCED-WORKER-QUEUE-PROOF-001) was already fixed: 9 post_dispatch_maintenance discards in 3 hours, with health evidence age at 272s against the 300s threshold. The failure was externally silent: metrics showed the phase executed, cycles had no error, watchdog reported healthy; only one activity-log line (runtime_phase_cas_conflict) per discard showed anything.
failure_reproduction.regression: test_recovery_contract_boundaries.py adds two tests: one proves a delivery-health observation survives a same-cycle rejected worker/queue transition (it must not be discarded by a write it does not participate in), and one proves a phase that keeps losing its CAS emits a console escalation once SUSTAINED_PHASE_DISCARD_THRESHOLD consecutive discards accumulate. Both tests fail on the unmodified base and pass with this change.

implementation.new_phase_added: DELIVERY_HEALTH_OBSERVATION_PHASE = "delivery_health_observations", run as its own _run_reserved_runtime_phase transaction via commit_delivery_health_observations(), called from run_once() ahead of apply_post_dispatch_maintenance
implementation.discard_visibility_added: record_reserved_phase_outcome(phase_name, committed=...) tracks a per-phase consecutive-discard streak in _PHASE_DISCARD_STREAKS, resets on any commit, and _run_reserved_runtime_phase logs a console_log escalation once the streak reaches SUSTAINED_PHASE_DISCARD_THRESHOLD (3)
implementation.existing_gates_preserved: _run_reserved_runtime_phase's canonical revalidation, CAS-conflict handling, and activity-log emission are unchanged; apply_post_dispatch_maintenance keeps its existing transition guard semantics and now receives delivery_health_observations=() since those are committed earlier
implementation.lock_cost: One additional short transaction per cycle: measured at 6 flock acquisitions and ~18ms against a cycle of roughly 30s, within the acceptance bound of one additional short transaction

passed.result: provisioned checkout-scoped .venv-pantheon; verified importable from a foreign cwd with no PYTHONPATH
28 passed (includes the 2 new regression tests for this task; both fail on the unmodified base)

broader_nonpassing_observations.note: The owner's original implementation note referenced 2 local pre-existing failures in this suite (test_crash_retry_window_outbox_committed_runner_terminated_receipt_retry and test_real_isolated_runner_stop_and_dispatch_flow), asserted to fail identically with and without this change. Re-running the full test_supervisor.py plus test_supervisor_recovery_process_e2e.py suites at the merged head (after rebasing onto origin/dev c6f39a8d8) in this closeout pass produced 0 failures (353 + 5 = 358 passed). This is consistent with the stated claim that those 2 were environment-flaky rather than caused by this change; no failure was observed to be introduced by this task in either run.

review_decision.note: Independently verify that the health-observation commit is decoupled from the maintenance CAS without weakening existing worker/queue transition guards, that the sustained-discard escalation fires at the configured threshold, and that the measured per-cycle lock cost stays within one additional short transaction.
